name: Raking
description: Raking uses a serrated or wavy pick moved rapidly back and forth under light tension to randomly set multiple pins simultaneously. It is faster than SPP but less reliable on quality locks. Raking is the preferred opening move when speed matters more than precision — entry points with low-grade cylinders (common in commercial and institutional settings) often open within seconds. It is typically the first technique attempted on any unknown lock before committing to SPP.

blue.det: Scratching around keyway; time at door without key; more visible tool manipulation than SPP.
blue.cm: Security pins make raking significantly less effective; high-security cylinders; access log monitoring.
